newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares close with another tumble.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares close with another tumble.

text.p: Nigerian shares maintained a downward trend with another sharp drop on Monday and pressure to sell showed no sign of abating, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 8019.95 from 8133.93 on Friday.
Traders said there was still no buying interest for shares in leading conglomerates, despite prices which have fallen substantially in recent weeks.
Analysts said the market's bearish trend has hit the blue chips most because of their higher prices, which make investors want to sell them for quick money.
Lever Brothers was down 41 kobo at 23.98 naira. PZ Industries slid to 24.00 naira, down 39 kobo and UAC UAC.LG fell to 13.80 naira, down 19 kobo.
Investors were unrelenting in selling shares of Cadbury, causing it to fall by 20 kobo to 33.20 naira.
Tyre firm Dunlop was down eight kobo to 9.42 naira.
Monday's other losers were Unipetrol, 30 kobo down at 63.70 naira, and Nigerian Breweries, five kobo lower at 16.65 naira.

But improved interest in the insurance sector saw AIICO rising 21 kobo to 15.72 naira after recent good results. An equally impressive result propelled traders to hike Prestige Assurance by five kobo to 6.40 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank was 13 kobo higher at 9.31 naira, followed by rally Union Bank which was five kobo up at 9.05 naira.
Guinness too climbed four kobo to 8.80 naira.
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham gained five kobo to end at 5.45 naira while Neimeth Pharmaceuticals also rose five kobo to close at 7.95 naira.
